section_summary: This section moves from a 1948 table of Japanese securities to 1949 correspondence about the Dodge Mission, Japanese-owned gold, and financial stabilization. Its largest group of documents concerns Joseph Dodge’s statements on Japan’s budget and the Japanese press response. Later items address trading in Japanese dollar securities and the disposition of gold held in Japan.

subfiles.title: Securities table attached to Tokyo despatch No. 213
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese railway, utility, industrial and other securities with quantities, dates and values.
subfiles.summary: Continuation of an attached securities table.

subfiles.title: The Dodge Mission to Japan
subfiles.about: Discusses Department representation on Dodge’s mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Notes that no available senior officer meets Dodge’s conditions for a Department representative.

subfiles.title: Protocol for Japanese GATT membership
subfiles.about: Reports preparations to raise a Japanese protocol at the GATT meeting in Annecy.
subfiles.summary: A separate protocol is being drafted; McCormick will answer questions from Wellington.

subfiles.title: Japanese Gold Pot
subfiles.about: Recommends opposing removal of Japanese-owned revolving-fund gold to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Barnett finds no legal bar to shipment but cites political, psychological and economic objections.

subfiles.title: Japanese Gold Pot, duplicate copy
subfiles.about: Duplicates Barnett’s recommendation concerning removal of the revolving-fund gold.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the preceding memorandum, recommending Butterworth sign the letter and draft message.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning the OJEIRF Gold Pot
subfiles.about: Seeks Army concurrence in a draft message advising against shipment of Japanese gold.
subfiles.summary: Butterworth forwards State’s position and proposed message to Dodge.

subfiles.title: Draft message to Dodge on transferring the Gold Pot
subfiles.about: Sets out objections to transferring Japanese-owned gold to the United States.
subfiles.summary: The draft cites adverse political impressions, limits on returning the gold, transport and insurance costs, and little prospect of a higher U.S. assay value.

subfiles.title: Removal of Gold Pot to United States
subfiles.about: Records Robert West’s disagreement with State’s economic objections to moving the gold.
subfiles.summary: A March 28 addendum records agreement to delete the draft cable’s third paragraph.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Statement on Japanese Budget by Minister Joseph M. Dodge and Editorial Comment Thereon
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits Dodge’s April 15 budget statement and reports Japanese press reactions.
subfiles.summary: The despatch outlines Dodge’s call for a balanced consolidated budget, stronger tax collection, visible and declining subsidies, and supervised use of the aid Counterpart Fund. It summarizes Japanese editorials on austerity, monetary policy and overdue government payments, concluding that fiscal reform is essential to stabilization.

subfiles.title: US Will Judge Japan by Actions, Not Words
subfiles.about: Reports speculation that U.S. aid might be reconsidered if Japan fails to curb deficit spending.
subfiles.summary: The article anticipates a review of Japanese stabilization efforts within six months.

subfiles.title: The Nature of the Budget
subfiles.about: Praises Dodge’s criticism of opaque budgets and subsidies.
subfiles.summary: The editorial argues that a clearer budget will help taxpayers understand fiscal policy and support lasting reform.

subfiles.title: Extracts from Japanese-language editorials on Dodge’s budget statement
subfiles.from: Tokyo Shimbun; Nihon Keizai; Sekai Keizai; Mainichi; Jiji Shimpo; Asahi; Yomiuri
subfiles.about: Collects Japanese newspaper responses to Dodge’s April 15 budget statement.
subfiles.summary: The editorials discuss austerity, the balanced budget, U.S. aid, subsidies, the Counterpart Fund and banknote policy. Asahi stresses overdue government payments; Yomiuri urges politicians and citizens to face Japan’s financial situation.

subfiles.title: Statement on the Japanese budget
subfiles.about: Explains the balanced 1949 budget and its role in the Nine Point Stabilization Program.
subfiles.summary: Dodge describes prior deficits and concealed subsidies, calls for better tax collection and spending restraint, and explains the consolidated budget. He presents the Counterpart Fund as a supervised means to retire debt and finance productive investment without renewed inflation.

subfiles.title: Comment on Statement on Japanese Budget issued April 15, 1949 by Financial Adviser Dodge
subfiles.about: Reports Reid’s account of how and why Dodge’s budget statement was prepared.
subfiles.summary: Reid says Ikeda concurred and the statement was timed to Diet debate and Communist criticism.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Dodge press statements
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of Dodge’s press statements at Robert West’s direction.
subfiles.summary: Cover letter for the enclosed press statements.

subfiles.title: Draft acknowledgement of Dodge press statements
subfiles.about: Thanks the Army office for sending Dodge’s press statements.
subfiles.summary: Brief draft acknowledgement of the May 31 enclosure.

subfiles.title: Press Statements: Joseph M. Dodge
subfiles.about: Introduces a compilation of Dodge’s press statements.
subfiles.summary: Title page for statements by Dodge as U.S. minister and financial adviser.

subfiles.title: Press statement of March 7, 1949
subfiles.about: Addresses currency, exchange rates, inflation and Japanese economic self-support.
subfiles.summary: Dodge disavows an existing plan for currency devaluation and calls for a durable exchange rate. He urges fiscal restraint, increased production, lower costs and exports so Japan can eventually replace U.S. aid.

subfiles.title: Press statement of April 15, 1949
subfiles.about: Presents Dodge’s full account of the consolidated 1949 budget and stabilization measures.
subfiles.summary: Dodge calls the balanced budget the first requirement of stabilization and explains earlier deficits, tax collection failures and subsidies hidden in foreign trade accounts. He says the new Counterpart Fund will be supervised by SCAP and used chiefly for debt retirement and productive investment.

subfiles.title: Press statement of May 2, 1949
subfiles.about: Acknowledges cooperation with the Dodge Mission’s stabilization work.
subfiles.summary: Dodge thanks MacArthur and his command for support and says MacArthur was kept informed of recommendations.

subfiles.title: Press statement of May 14, 1949
subfiles.about: Reviews the mission’s economic measures after Dodge’s return to San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: Dodge cites the balanced budget, reduced subsidies, Counterpart Fund, single exchange rate and tighter raw-material allocation as steps toward Japanese self-support.

subfiles.title: Trading in Japanese dollar securities
subfiles.from: Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Army
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP’s views on resuming U.S. trading in Japanese dollar securities.
subfiles.summary: The message favors quoted markets and asks whether SCAP rules need a general license or amendment.

subfiles.title: Disposition of gold held in Japan earmarked for France and Thailand
subfiles.about: Records approval of a proposed course of action for earmarked gold.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary approves the proposed letter and SCAP directive, subject to Army coordination and legal revision.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Dodge’s letter to Ikeda
subfiles.about: Forwards a Dodge letter and promises copies of its final version.
subfiles.summary: Reid sends an attachment and says Dodge is preparing the final letter to Minister Ikeda.
